A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same controlled Table QA study. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on paired table representations, diagnostic comparisons, verbalization ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds table-width results, Gemini-2.5-Pro evaluations and a human check of evaluator judgments.

M1.justification: The column-selection, template-construction and serialization pipeline in Section 3.1 is unchanged, as are the Appendix A prompts. Naming the benchmark REPAIRTQA and adding a method-selection diagram do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use BIRD, TableEval and MMQA with the same seven diagnostic splits. The width analysis partitions existing BIRD coverage, and Gemini-2.5-Pro uses the retained tasks; neither establishes a new dataset, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro to the comparisons across S1–S5 and M1–M2 in Tables 6 and 7. The original seven comparison methods retain their participation in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: v2 introduces width strata of 1–5, 6–20 and over 20 columns, plus a randomly sampled 100-case human evaluator audit. Existing split specifications, judge and prompts remain unchanged. The width counts total 873 versus 866 BIRD instances implied by Table 1; this unexplained discrepancy does not establish revised underlying coverage.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends validation through a new width-sensitivity analysis, a Gemini-2.5-Pro check of generality across stronger models, and human validation of the evaluator. These examine previously untested aspects of the study's reliability; the earlier verbalization ablations and case-study findings are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly estimates evaluator reliability through human–LLM agreement on 100 random cases, reporting 96% agreement. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for benchmark accuracies; the agreement check does not establish additional benchmark runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets for width buckets and Gemini-2.5-Pro across all seven splits, plus the 96% evaluator agreement result. For example, Gemini-2.5-Pro newly scores 76.59% structured and 73.86% semi-structured on S3. Existing aggregate and matched split accuracies are unchanged; two illustrative wrong-answer IDs are removed from the long-table case discussion.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The new width categories are empirical stratification rules, and Section 6's call for future mechanistic and theoretical analysis adds no mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: controlled representation pairing, a diagnostic benchmark, paradigm-dependent trade-offs and no universally best method. The benchmark name and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 turns broad deployment guidance into specific method-selection rules and acknowledges unresolved mechanisms. Section 2.2 explicitly limits scope to tables fitting current context windows, while Appendix C adds explanations involving column selection and symbolic execution. Existing interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository access link below the abstract, whereas v1 only promises a future release. Existing prompts, model identifiers and implementation descriptions are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, but not the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged after matching pagination and section renumbering. The claimed novelty of a controlled, same-information comparison across representations and method families is retained.

P1.justification: v2 names the benchmark REPAIRTQA, inserts a Discussion and Future Work section and two analytical appendices, and makes localized explanatory edits. Most existing prose, contributions, prompts, related work and conclusion remain unchanged rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds the decision tree in Figure 8 and Tables 4–6, and expands the former Table 4 into Table 7 with Gemini-2.5-Pro rows. Existing charts and case-study graphics are retained, with localized relocation, renumbering and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The human check provides limited direct support for the evaluator underlying all comparisons, while the width and Gemini-2.5-Pro analyses improve diagnostic depth. The code pointer and scope qualifications also help. These gains are tempered by unexplained width-sample accounting and overbroad new guidance: Figure 8 recommends hybrids for short semi-structured compositional queries, although Table 7 gives Gemini-2.5-Pro 73.86% on S3 versus Weaver's 49.66%.
